transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-23 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ashley Romero (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (Mosaic CTO), Marcus Green (Lead ML Eng), Priya Rao (SRE), Owen Park (Product)

Summary section (auto): quick notes - Mosaic wants to get running fast with free credits, wants guidance for hosted vs private because of client data residency + internal security review, wants to understand latency and cost expected for their 200ms p95 target.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Ashley Romero: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Ashley, AE on the Redwood account. we got Samir and Leah from SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dana Liu: Doing well, thanks. excited to get this going. we've poked at a few models locally but want to see how Redwood's hosted path could shorten time to first token.
[00:17] Marcus Green: yeah hi, Marcus here. main question: can we go from repo to first usable API call within a day using credits? also curious about dedicated or VPC for later.
[00:29] Ashley Romero: Great, that's exactly what the quickstart is for. our free credits + quickstart SDKs are usually enough to get a prototype running same day. Samir, want to add details on the dev flow?
[00:38] Samir Patel: sure. typically you sign up, we provision sandbox tokens, you can hit the hosted API with an open model or our curated variants. sample app + SDK, the usual. people hit first call in a couple hours, time to first meaningful token depends on prompt set and model.
[00:54] Priya Rao: quick question on data — during the trial, are requests logged or retained? we have clients with PII so retention policy matters.
[01:02] Samir Patel: good question. hosted default keeps telemetry for debugging but we can enable tenancy options, and we have short retention options in the console, also enterprise private deploys give you customer-controlled logs. I'll follow up with the security doc.
[01:16] Owen Park: when you say 'private', do you mean on-prem, or VPC peering? different teams mean different things.
[01:22] Leah Chen: we mean both. Redwood Private can be VPC (customer VPC peering) or an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. most customers start hosted for speed and then move to dedicated or private when they require isolation or residency.
[01:36] Marcus Green: OK. for our use case, we expect mid-tier throughput — maybe 50 qps peak for inference with short responses. our SLA needs p95 < 250ms for user-facing features. is that realistic on hosted?
[01:48] Samir Patel: depends on model and token lengths. For smaller open models we often hit sub-200ms p95 with the right instance type and batching config, for larger models you're looking at higher latency. we can provide a recommended model/quantization profile and kernel selection. Also worth talking about batching: it reduces cost but can increase tail latency.
[02:09] Dana Liu: are there sample benchmarks that show hosted cost per 1k tokens versus dedicated? we need to make a show-back to finance.
[02:16] Ashley Romero: yes, we'll share a simple cost comparison (hosted PAYG vs dedicated reserved) and a model selection cheat sheet. i'll include an example cost calc using your expected qps and token lengths.
[02:27] Priya Rao: security checklist: SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO support, KMS integration for key management, audit logs. Are those supported out of the box for the hosted tier?
[02:36] Leah Chen: hosted has SOC2, SSO integration via SAML, and audit logs for workspace actions; for KMS customer-managed keys are typically a Private/Dedicated feature. we do offer bring-your-own-key for Private in VPC deployments.
[02:48] Marcus Green: good. latency wise, we will likely want to bench p50/p95 and token costs. can we run a micro-benchmark using our prompt set in your sandbox?
[02:57] Samir Patel: absolutely. typical flow: you drop a small prompt set and we'll run a 10k token throughput run on a similar instance as hosted; we'll return p50/p95 and cost per token. that data usually helps in deciding hosted vs dedicated.
[03:11] Dana Liu: timeline: we want to prove this in two weeks and make a hosting decision in three. can Redwood support that cadence?
[03:18] Ashley Romero: yes — quickstart + sandbox can be done day-of, bench in a few days, then a pilot for 2 weeks. if you sign up for credits today, you'll have runway for the bench and a short pilot.
[03:26] Owen Park: any gotchas with our infra? we run EKS, and some of our services are in eu-west-1 region. we care about regional routing.
[03:34] Leah Chen: we have hosted regions in us-west-2, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast variants. routing can be configured by account, and for Dedicated we can pin pools to regions.
[03:43] Marcus Green: competitor question — we've looked at Anthropic & Vertex for managed endpoints. can Redwood handle model variants and graceful fallback if capacity is constrained?
[03:51] Samir Patel: yes. smart routing and automatic fallbacks are part of the platform — you can set policies to prefer a lower-cost variant and fallback to a larger model or different region if needed.
[04:02] Priya Rao: re: compliance, we may need a BAA for certain customers. Is that something Redwood supports for Private customers?
[04:09] Leah Chen: BAAs are part of our enterprise contract packages, typically paired with Private deployments where customer data residency and isolation are required. we'll connect you to our legal/sales ops for details.
[04:19] Marcus Green: Operational question: how do you handle caching and prefix reuse? we use long-running chat sessions where KV cache matters.
[04:28] Samir Patel: runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching features; for high-throughput chat we advise a configuration that keeps the KV cache warm on the same pool. we'll show config examples in the runbook.
[04:40] Dana Liu: great. cost optimization: any low-effort levers?
[04:44] Ashley Romero: quantization profiles, batching, and prefix caching are top levers. Redwood Optimize recommendations will suggest batching window and model quantization given your workload.
[04:53] Marcus Green: ok, next step for bench — what's the artifact we should send? just prompts + expected concurrency?
[04:58] Samir Patel: prompt set, token length estimate, expected concurrency pattern (p50/p95 goals), and any regional constraints — that's enough. we'll run bench and return a simple spreadsheet showing p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:11] Owen Park: last question for time: what's the commercial for credits — do credits expire? and how do reserved commitments work?
[05:18] Ashley Romero: credits usually have a 90-day expiry for trials; reserved capacity is monthly/annual commit with discounts and SLA guarantees. we'll include a pricing summary in the follow-up doc.
[05:28] Dana Liu: sounds good. to recap, we'll get the sandbox tokens + quickstart, send a prompt set, Redwood runs bench, then we decide hosted vs private w/in 3 weeks?
[05:37] Ashley Romero: yes, and i'll include a suggested pilot plan + checklist.
[05:42] Priya Rao: I'd like to schedule a technical deep dive with your infra folks if the bench looks good.
[05:48] Samir Patel: happy to — we'll set aside an hour and bring our runtime lead.
[05:52] Marcus Green: one small nit: sometimes transcripts swap 'KV cache' to 'kay vee cache' or similar — hope that was captured.
[05:58] Leah Chen: noted. we'll attach a written runbook and config snippets to avoid confusion.
[06:04] Ashley Romero: great. we'll follow up with the sandbox key and docs. thanks everyone.
[06:08] Dana Liu: thanks, bye.
